ops.description:
daemonkit moves per-daemon state from the non-hidden `~/<label>/` to `~/.daemonkit/agents/<label>/` (new `paths.Agent(label)`; `daemon.go:56`). **Breaking at runtime, no migration by decision** — old state is wiped rather than migrated, on every host.

**CORRECTED 2026-08-16:** an earlier version of this task listed 10 consumers. The authoritative list is **13**, taken from `daemonkit/.github/workflows/fleet-build.yml`'s matrix and `daemonkit/ci/fleet-refs.txt` (which refuses a file that omits any consumer). The four I originally missed are **reposync, cc-notes, binrun, cookiesync**.

| consumer | daemonkit |
|---|---|
| cc-pool | v0.21.4 |
| fusekit | v0.21.4 |
| cc-interact | v0.21.4 |
| cc-skills/plugins/codex (codex-ask) | v0.21.4 |
| cc-notes | v0.21.3 |
| synckit | v0.21.2 |
| captain-hook | v0.21.2 |
| cc-orchestrate | v0.21.2 |
| cc-present | v0.21.2 |
| reposync | v0.21.2 |
| cookiesync | v0.21.2 |
| cc-review | v0.21.1 |
| cc-patch | v0.21.0 |
| **binrun** | **v0.17.2** |

`binrun` is four minor versions behind and is also the fleet's **linux canary** (its fleet-refs line builds `darwin,linux`), so it is the leg most likely to surprise. Note `cc-skills/plugins/codex` is not a fleet-build leg but is a real consumer.

**The release gate, and the escape hatch.** `fleet-build.yml` compiles every consumer against the daemonkit tree via a generated `go.work` overlay, on every push to main and every PR, "so a breaking surface change goes red before a release exists." For a breaking change the mechanism is `ci/fleet-refs.txt`: point each consumer's leg at the branch carrying that consumer's migration while it is in flight, so the gate measures the tree about to merge rather than a main still pinning the old daemonkit. A ref must name a branch or tag — never a commit (cone peers are fetched with `git clone --branch`).

Note the state-root move is **behavioral, not API-shaped** — `paths.Socket` keeps its signature and `paths.Agent` is additive — so fleet-build may well stay green on the daemonkit push itself. The ordering pain is the reverse direction: fusekit's and cc-pool's new code *requires* the new daemonkit, so those legs need migration branches.

**Hosts:** this machine and `yasyf-forge-studio` (Tailscale `100.113.56.52`, key auth works, same label dirs). 13 non-hidden `~/com.*` dirs and 14 LaunchAgents to unload/wipe/reload.

**Packaging is not uniform.** `ccp` ships via a Homebrew formula (`Cellar/cc-pool`); `codex-ask` ships via a Homebrew **Cask** (`Caskroom/codex-ask`, from yasyf/homebrew-tap). Those need releases, not a local `go build`.

**Hard prerequisite.** cc-pool `4a3881b` notes the trust requirement compiles into `CCPoolStatus.app`, so 0.65.0's runtime refuses the drain: **bootout the agent before installing over it**, or Supersede fails at "land packaged candidate" with ErrUntrusted.

**Deploy order is forced:** daemonkit release → fusekit release → cc-pool widget rebuild (its `project.yml` pins SPM deps by released version, so it cannot build before both) → verify `ccp add` → fleet migration → wipe both hosts.

**Watch out for** the existing cc-notes item on cask-installed daemonkit binaries hanging pre-main under kernel provenance tracking (codex-ask, reposync) — the same binaries this migration reinstalls.

Socket-path budget: `sunPathBytes = 104`; the move adds 18 bytes. On `/Users/yasyf` the longest real label (`com.github.yasyf.synckit.serve`, 73b) keeps ~30b headroom; a long username plus a long reverse-DNS label is the squeeze case.
